newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks stretch gains, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks stretch gains, seen steady.

text.p: Argentine stocks continued their mild rally Friday on foreign buy orders and were seen pushing higher early next week.
Brokers said the slow pace of trading induced by a general strike launched midday Thursday was offset by higher turnover in emerging market equities on Wall Street.
"Stocks are firm and tested resistance levels again today, but since volumes are low in Buenos Aires the market is pretty restrained," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV advanced 0.9 percent to 555.65, extending gains this week to 1.4 percent.
The MerVal shows a 9.1 percent gain so far in September and stands at a 10-week high.
"Industrial production data is fuelling the rise in stocks, but the real motor of the market these days is the rally in government bonds," said Daneri.
He argued bond prices were almost discounting a long-term debt buyback plan, even though Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said in New York Friday no such scheme was imminent.
Fernandez, who spoke after Argentina announced a 10-year, $750 million global bond issue, said only a Brady debt swap was under study as part of his 1996 funding strategy.

In the session floor volume eased to 11.6 million pesos from 12 million Thursday. Over-the-counter deals, however, surged to a healthy tally of 180.3 million pesos from 50.6 million Thursday due to end-of-month position-squaring and a raft of foreign purchases, dealers said.
The broad market index closed 0.7 percent higher Friday, with winners whipping losers 35 to four and 16 stocks closing unchanged.
The only main-tier losers were steelmaker Acindar and agricultural holding company Capex, which shed 0.9 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively.

Best MerVal performers were carmaker Ciadea, which jumped 4.5 percent, sugar refiner Ledesma, which gained 2.6 percent, pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which closed up 2.3 percent, and steelmaker Siderca, up 2.1 percent.
